content: Ribavirin is not effective in treating hepatitis C unless it is used in combination with another medication. If you have hepatitis C, your doctor will prescribe an additional medication to take alongside ribavirin. It is crucial to take both medications exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. Ribavirin can cause anemia, a condition characterized by a reduction in red blood cells. Inform your doctor if you have a history of heart attack, high blood pressure, breathing problems, or blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia (a genetic condition where red blood cells are abnormally shaped and cannot deliver oxygen effectively) or thalassemia (a condition where red blood cells lack sufficient hemoglobin to carry oxygen). Also, notify your doctor if you have or have had heart disease. If you experience symptoms such as extreme fatigue, pale skin, headache, dizziness, confusion, rapid heartbeat, weakness, shortness of breath, or chest pain, contact your doctor immediately. It is essential to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory for monitoring. Blood tests will be conducted before starting ribavirin and frequently during the first four weeks of treatment. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide you with a Medication Guide from the manufacturer when you begin treatment with ribavirin and each time you refill your prescription. Read this information carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. You can also access the Medication Guide on the FDA website. Discuss the risks of taking ribavirin with your doctor. For female patients: Do not take ribavirin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. A pregnancy test must confirm that you are not pregnant before starting ribavirin. You must use two forms of birth control and undergo monthly pregnancy tests during treatment and for six months afterward. If you become pregnant during this time, contact your doctor immediately. Ribavirin can cause severe harm or death to the fetus. For male patients: Do not take ribavirin if your partner is pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If your partner can become pregnant, ensure a pregnancy test confirms she is not pregnant before starting ribavirin. Use two forms of birth control, including a condom with spermicide, during treatment and for six months afterward. Your partner must undergo monthly pregnancy tests during this period. If your partner becomes pregnant, contact your doctor immediately. Ribavirin can cause severe harm or death to the fetus. Ribavirin is prescribed in combination with another medication, such as an interferon, to treat hepatitis C. It belongs to a class of antiviral medications called nucleoside analogues, which work by preventing the hepatitis C virus from spreading within the body. However, it is not known whether ribavirin-based treatment cures hepatitis C, prevents liver damage caused by the virus, or stops the spread of hepatitis C to others. Ribavirin is available as tablets, capsules, and an oral solution. It is typically taken twice daily, in the morning and evening, for 24–48 weeks or longer. Tablets should be taken with food, while capsules and oral solutions should also be taken with food unless your doctor advises otherwise. If instructed to take ribavirin without food, ensure you take it the same way every day. It is best to take ribavirin at the same times each day. Follow the prescription label instructions carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the oral solution well before each use and clean the measuring spoon or cup after each use. If side effects occur, your doctor may adjust your dose or temporarily stop the medication. Do not alter your dose or stop taking ribavirin without your doctor’s approval. Ribavirin is sometimes used to treat viral hemorrhagic fevers (viruses causing internal and external bleeding, organ failure, and death) or severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), which can cause breathing problems, pneumonia, and death. It may also be used in cases of biological warfare to treat deliberately spread viral hemorrhagic fever. Discuss the potential risks of using ribavirin for your condition with your doctor. Before taking ribavirin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ribavirin or any other medications. If taking ribavirin tablets, mention if you are allergic to corn. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. This includes medications for anxiety, depression, mental illness, HIV/AIDS (e.g., didanosine, stavudine, zidovudine), or immune suppression (e.g., chemotherapy, cyclosporine, sirolimus, tacrolimus). If taking ribavirin capsules, inform your doctor if you are using antacids. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you consume large amounts of alcohol, use street drugs, have had suicidal thoughts or attempts, or have undergone an organ transplant. Also, disclose any history of mental illness (e.g., depression, anxiety, psychosis), cancer, psoriasis, HIV/AIDS, diabetes, sarcoidosis, Gilbert’s syndrome, gout, liver disease (other than hepatitis C), or thyroid, kidney, pancreas, eye, or lung disease. If you have previously taken medication for hepatitis C, ensure your doctor has your complete medical records and knows how you responded to past treatments. Do not breastfeed while taking ribavirin. Ribavirin may cause drowsiness, dizziness, or confusion. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Do not consume alcohol while taking ribavirin, as it can worsen liver disease. Drink plenty of fluids while taking ribavirin. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, contact your doctor for guidance. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Mild side effects of ribavirin include cough, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, heartburn, loss of appetite, weight loss, changes in taste, dry mouth, difficulty concentrating, insomnia, memory loss, rash, dry or itchy skin, sweating, irregular menstruation, muscle or bone pain, and hair loss. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Severe side effects include hives, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, difficulty swallowing or breathing, stomach or lower back pain, bloody diarrhea, bright red or black stools, unusual bleeding or bruising, vision changes, fever, chills, signs of infection, depression, suicidal thoughts, mood changes, excessive worry, irritability, relapse into substance abuse, worsening psoriasis, and intolerance to cold. Ribavirin may also slow growth and weight gain in children. Discuss the risks of giving this medication to your child with their doctor. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store ribavirin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep tablets and capsules at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Oral solutions can be stored in the refrigerator or at room temperature. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
